_about: T679 #12 (moved from `deliver/export/closures.py`, 2026-11-20): the owner's rulings on the export's two closure scans (`closures._closure_scan`), one row per (entry_id, rule_id) with why it is the book. `release`: a DATED WATER RELEASE that speaks while a blanket closure of its region also speaks can never apply - how a missed exemption shows (the Nicola, RU-2); `quota`: a WATER ROW'S KEEPING QUOTA in force that a blanket zone closure silences (review F5; since RU-7 such a quota vanishes from the page). The export refuses a finding not listed here (`closures.release_under_closure_problems`); each listed `why` ships as the finding's `known`. Every reason is read under the STRICT LIFT RULING (2026-10-05): a zone closure and a water's row both hold - closed on the union of their dates - and a row beats the closure only where the book prints an exemption or a dated release/opening/quota INSIDE it. `left`: rows taken off a list, and why (history, read by people). Written by hand (each row is a ruling); read by the export only (`closures.under_closure_calls`).

release.why: the Duck Lake row's bass catch and release (May 15-Jun 15) binds the STREAM sections of the entry's water (its tributary creeks), under Region 4's Apr 1-Jun 14 stream closure: both hold, and the creeks stay closed to Jun 14 (user decision 2026-10-05: the row's release does not lift the stream closure); the lake itself is not a stream

quota.why: the row's own Oct 1-May 31 closure and Region 3's Jan 1-Jun 30 spring stream closure both hold (the user's own example of the union); only the printed 'Additional opening May 1-31' lifts, on exactly those dates — so June is closed and the 2 per day holds from Jul 1

Region 3's Jan 1-Jun 30 spring stream closure holds on the whole river: below the lake beside the row's own 'No Fishing Jan 1-May 31' (closed to Jun 30 — the p.28 list is a steelhead closure list, no exemption; user decision 2026-10-05), above it alone; the quota holds Jul 1-Dec 31

tributaries only: the mainstem row prints 'tributaries subject to spring closure', so Region 6's Fraser-watershed stream closure (Apr 1-Jun 30) holds on them and no lift reaches a tributary (user decision 2026-10-05); the 1 per day holds the rest of the year
tributaries only: as Region 6's — Zone 7A's spring stream closure holds on them ('tributaries subject to spring closure'); the 1 per day holds the rest of the year

the park's streams lying in Zone 7A fall under Zone 7A's spring stream closure: Region 5's page exception (p.42) lifts only Region 5's closure, and the row prints no exemption Zone 7A's tables list; its lakes keep the 1 per day

bass 'no limit' on all CVWMA waters, undated: it lifts Region 4's bass CLOSURE (named fish), never the Apr 1-Jun 14 stream closure on its stream/slough sections (sloughs are streams, 2026-10-02) — both hold
bass 8 per day, undated, on a stream under Region 8's spring stream closure outside the reaches the row prints exempt: both hold, closed Apr 1-Jun 30
bass 8 per day, undated, under Region 8's spring stream closure: no printed exemption, both hold

the Duck Lake row's bass quota on its tributary creeks (STREAM sections) under Region 4's Apr 1-Jun 14 stream closure: both hold, the creeks are closed to Jun 14 (user decision 2026-10-05: leave as built); the lake is not a stream
the same Duck Lake creeks: the bass size clause under the stream closure
a slough is a stream (2026-10-02): Region 4's Apr 1-Jun 14 stream closure holds; the row's undated quota lifts the bass CLOSURE (named fish), not the stream closure
a slough is a stream (2026-10-02): as French Slough

the hatchery steelhead 2 is silenced by the row's OWN Mar 16-May 31 closure (RU-3) on the days Region 6's steelhead stream closure (May 15-Jun 15, its own exemption list printed — the Kitimat is not on it) also holds

the trout/char 1 per day, asked for a steelhead May 15-Jun 15: Region 6's steelhead stream closure holds on the river's Region 6 pieces (its exemptions are the Skeena, Nass, Iskut, Stikine and Taku mainstems only, p.49); the row lifts nothing for it

the trout/char 1 per day, for a steelhead under Region 6's May 15-Jun 15 steelhead stream closure: 'open all year' lifts only the full winter closure, never a species closure (G4, user decision 2026-10-05)
as Station Creek: 'open all year' never lifts Region 6's steelhead stream closure
as Station Creek: 'open all year' never lifts Region 6's steelhead stream closure
the park's possession clause beside its 1 per day (r1, above): the same Zone 7A spring stream closure on the park's streams
yellow perch 'no limit' beside the bass (r1, above): the same Region 4 Apr 1-Jun 14 stream closure on the CVWMA's stream/slough sections

the owner's P7b ruling (2026-11-26, T1177, RULINGS L28), the lower Quesnel: "Yes, close it too (Recommended)": the Quesnel River below the Cariboo River (about 99.9 km) keeps Region 5's Apr 1-June 30 spring stream closure, because below the Cariboo the row prints only catch and release, this quota and a bait ban, no closure of its own and no 'open all year' (its 'No Fishing upstream of Cariboo River, Mar 1-June 15' lifts the closure above the Cariboo only); the 1 per day (none under 40 cm) downstream of Morehead Creek holds Jul 1-Mar 31 on the river below the Cariboo

the rainbow 2 per day (none over 35 cm), asked for a steelhead Jan 1-Jun 30 (RULINGS S15 (owner 2026-11-27, Buckley Creek: "Release: the row's cap holds (Recommended)"): a water row's rainbow cap holds for the steelhead, so this rule is asked about it): Region 3's 'ALL STEELHEAD' release names the steelhead and beats the cap by naming (the ladder, as S12's size-free rule), on days Region 3's Jan 1-June 30 spring stream closure also holds, so the river reads closed; below the old Clearwater Bridge (exempt from the spring closure) the steelhead is released; the 2 per day holds for a rainbow up to 35 cm. The owner, 2026-11-27, asked "Clearwater River (Region 3). What changes for the angler: NOTHING. Before and after: Jan 1-Jun 30 closed; Aug 1 steelhead released, rainbow keep 2 (none over 35 cm). OK to mark this row as checked by you?": "Yes, mark it checked (Recommended)"

downstream of Goodwin Falls: the rainbow 2 per day (none over 35 cm), asked for a steelhead (RULINGS S15 (owner 2026-11-27, Buckley Creek: "Release: the row's cap holds (Recommended)"): a water row's rainbow cap holds for the steelhead, so this rule is asked about it): the row's OWN 'No Fishing Jan 1-June 30' closes the river on the days Region 3's Jan 1-June 30 spring stream closure also holds (the row closing itself, the DENETIAH shape); the 2 per day holds from Jul 1. The owner, 2026-11-27, asked "Mahood River below Goodwin Falls (Region 3). What changes for the angler: NOTHING. Before and after: Jan 1-Jun 30 closed (the row's own closure); Aug 1 steelhead released, rainbow keep 2 (none over 35 cm). OK to mark this row as checked by you?": "Yes, mark it checked (Recommended)"

the rainbow 1 per day (none over 50 cm), asked for a steelhead May 15-Jun 15 (RULINGS S15 (owner 2026-11-27, Buckley Creek: "Release: the row's cap holds (Recommended)"): a water row's rainbow cap holds for the steelhead, so this rule is asked about it): Region 6's steelhead stream closure (May 15-June 15, p.49; its exemptions are the Skeena, Nass, Iskut, Stikine and Taku mainstems, not Buckley Creek) holds, as for Station Creek: the row lifts nothing for the steelhead; outside it a steelhead over 50 cm is released (the cap) and the rainbow 1 per day holds. The owner, 2026-11-27, asked "Buckley Creek (Region 6). ONE change, the one you ruled today: Aug 1, hatchery steelhead: keep 1 -> RELEASE (the row's "none over 50 cm" holds). Unchanged: May 15-Jun 15 steelhead closed; wild steelhead released; rainbow keep 1. OK to mark this row as checked by you?": "Yes, mark it checked (Recommended)"

left.why: under the DENETIAH ruling the row's own 'No Fishing Jan 1-June 30' silences its quota - the water closing itself, not a zone closure hiding a missed exemption; `_closure_scan` counts such a quota as speaking (2026-11-27, T1250: back on the `quota` list: under RULINGS S15 the scan asks this cap about the steelhead, where the row's own 'No Fishing' wins for the steelhead by the ladder, not as `water_closure`, so it is a finding again; the owner checked it the same day)
under T13 (owner D4, 2026-10-12, ce74eaef) the ✱ row's "Exempt from spring closure" walks to its tributaries with its quotas, so Region 4's stream closure no longer silences the 5 rainbow there
